clean_filter.title: Clean the filter
clean_filter.why: The filter keeps fine dust in the bin. Once its pleats are clogged, suction drops and the robot picks up less.
steps: Press the bin release and take the bin out of the robot.
Lift the filter out by its tab.
Tap it against the inside of a waste bin until no more dust falls out. Do not brush the pleats.
Put the filter back with the pleats facing the same way, and slide the bin in until it clicks.
clean_filter.caution: Never wash a paper filter or let it get wet: once wet, it no longer filters.

steps: Press the bin release and pull the bin out of the robot.
Release the filter by pressing it down, then lift it out.
Tap it against the inside of a waste bin until no more dust falls out. Do not brush the pleats.
Put the filter back and slide the bin in until it clicks.
Press the bin release, take the bin out and empty it.
Press the tab of the filter door and lift the door.
Pull the filter out by its yellow tab and tap it against the inside of a waste bin until no more dust falls out.
Put the filter back, close the filter door and slide the bin in until it clicks.
Press the bin release on the back of the robot and take the bin out.
Open the bin door over a waste bin and empty the bin.
Grip the filter at its sides, pull it out to the left and tap it against the inside of the waste bin until no more dust falls out.
Put the filter back and slide the bin into its guide until it clicks.
Press the release on the lid, open it and lift the bin out by its handle.
Hold the bin over a waste bin and press its release to empty it.
Open the filter door, pull the filter out by its loop and tap it against the inside of the waste bin.
Put the filter back and close the filter door: it only closes with the filter seated correctly. Put the bin back.

clean_brushes.title: Clean the main brushes
clean_brushes.why: The main brushes lift dirt from carpet and hard floor into the bin. Hair wound round them makes them slip and pick up less.
steps: Turn the robot over onto a soft surface.
Open the brush frame by its release tabs and lift both brushes out.
Pull off the end caps and remove hair and threads from the ends and axles. Cut wound hair along the groove.
Put the end caps back, insert each brush where its shape fits, and close the frame.
clean_brushes.caution: The two brushes are not alike and fit only one way round. Do not force them.

steps: Turn the robot over onto a soft surface.
Lift the two yellow tabs of the brush frame and take out the bristle brush and the beater brush.
Pull off the end caps and remove hair and thread from the ends and the axles.
Put the end caps back, put each brush back where its shape fits and close the frame.
Turn the robot over onto a soft surface.
Squeeze the yellow tabs of the brush frame and fold the frame up.
Take out both rubber rollers, pull off the end caps and remove hair from the square and hexagonal pegs.
Put the end caps back, put each roller back where its peg fits and close the frame until it clicks.
Turn the robot over onto a soft surface.
Press the release button next to the brushes and open the brush frame.
Take out both rubber rollers, pull off the end caps and remove hair from the ends and the axles.
Put the end caps back, put each roller back where its shape fits and close the frame.
Turn the robot over onto a soft surface.
Press the button on the right of the cleaning head: the latch lifts.
Take out both rubber rollers, pull off the end caps and remove hair from the ends and the axles.
Put the end caps back, put the rollers back where their shape fits and close the latch.

clean_side_brush.title: Clean the side brush
clean_side_brush.why: The side brush sweeps dirt from edges and corners into the robot's path. Tangled or bent arms leave it behind.
steps: Turn the robot over.
Undo the screw in the middle of the brush, or pull the brush off where it has no screw.
Remove hair from the arms and the hub, and straighten bent bristles.
Fit the brush back onto its shaft and fasten it.
clean_side_brush.caution: Replace a brush whose arms are bent out of shape: it no longer reaches the edge.

s.title: Clean the corner brush
s.why: The corner brush sweeps dirt out of corners and along edges into the robot's path. Tangled or bent arms leave it behind.
steps: Turn the robot over.
Undo the screw with a small screwdriver and take the corner brush off.
Remove hair from the arms and the drive peg.
Put the brush back on the peg and tighten the screw again.
s.caution: Tighten the screw: a loose corner brush comes off while cleaning.

clean_wheel.title: Clean the wheels
clean_wheel.why: The front caster and the drive wheels carry the robot. Hair or grit in them makes it pull to one side or stop.
steps: Turn the robot over.
Pull the front caster out of its socket and take the wheel off its axle.
Remove hair and dirt from the wheel, the axle and the socket.
Turn the drive wheels by hand and clear anything that catches, then push the caster back in until it clicks.
clean_wheel.caution: Do not pull the drive wheels out: they are not meant to be removed.

s.why: The caster wheel at the back and the drive wheels carry the robot. Hair or grit in them makes it pull to one side or stop.
steps: Turn the robot over.
Pull the caster wheel at the back out of its socket and take the wheel off its axle.
Remove hair and dirt from the wheel, the axle and the socket.
Turn the drive wheels by hand and clear anything that catches, then push the caster back in until it clicks.

clean_cliff_sensors.title: Clean the cliff sensors
clean_cliff_sensors.why: The cliff sensors look down for stairs and drops. Dust on their windows can stop the robot or let it miss an edge.
steps: Turn the robot over.
Wipe each sensor window with a slightly damp melamine sponge or cloth.
Check that no window is scratched or covered.
clean_cliff_sensors.caution: Never spray a cleaning agent onto the sensors or into their openings.

clean_contact.title: Clean the charging contacts
clean_contact.why: The charging contacts on the robot and on the dock carry the charging current. A film on them interrupts charging.
steps: Lift the robot off the dock.
Rub the robot's charging contacts with a slightly damp melamine sponge or cloth until they shine.
Unplug the dock for 60 seconds and clean its contacts the same way.
Plug the dock back in and set the robot on it.
clean_contact.caution: Nothing abrasive and no metal tools. Contacts that are green, copper-coloured or sunk in are damaged: contact iRobot support.

steps: Lift the robot off the dock.
Rub the robot's charging contacts with a slightly damp melamine sponge or cloth until they shine.
Unplug the Home Base for 60 seconds and clean its contacts the same way. Wipe its docking sensor window with a dry cloth only.
Plug the Home Base back in and set the robot on it.
Lift the robot off the Clean Base.
Rub the robot's charging contacts with a slightly damp melamine sponge or cloth until they shine.
Unplug the Clean Base for 60 seconds and clean the contacts on its ramp the same way.
Plug the Clean Base back in and set the robot on it.
Lift the robot off the dock.
Rub the robot's charging contacts with a slightly damp melamine sponge or cloth until they shine.
Unplug the dock for 60 seconds. Wipe its contacts, the infrared window and the docking marker with a dry cloth only.
Plug the dock back in and set the robot on it.

clean_bin.title: Empty and check the bin
clean_bin.why: The bin holds what the robot picks up. A full or badly seated bin stops it from picking up more.
steps: Press the bin release and take the bin out.
Open the bin door over a waste bin and empty it.
Take the filter out, tap it clean and remove dust from the filter seat.
Put the filter back and slide the bin in until it clicks.
clean_bin.caution: Rinse only a bin made for it, with the filter taken out, and let it dry completely before it goes back.

steps: Press the bin release on the back of the robot and take the bin out.
Open the bin door over a waste bin and empty the bin.
Take the filter out and tap it clean. Rinse the bin by hand with warm water if it is dirty.
Let the bin dry completely, put the filter back and slide the bin in until it clicks.
eij.caution: Rinse by hand only, never in a dishwasher, and never with the filter in it.

steps: Press the release on the lid and lift the bin out by its handle.
Hold the bin over a waste bin and press its release to empty it.
Take the filter out and tap it clean. Rinse the bin with warm water if it is dirty.
Let the bin dry completely, put the filter back and the bin into the robot.
s.caution: Rinse by hand only, never in a dishwasher, and never with the filter in it.

clean_camera.title: Clean the camera window
clean_camera.why: The camera and the sensor windows help the robot find its way. Smudges make it lose its position.
steps: Find the camera window on top of or at the front of the robot.
Wipe it gently with a clean, dry microfibre cloth.
Wipe the other sensor windows at the front the same way.
clean_camera.caution: No liquids or cleaning agents on the windows.

clean_wash_dock.title: Clean the wash dock
clean_wash_dock.why: The wash dock rinses the mop. Dirt in its tray or a full dirty-water tank stops the washing.
steps: Take out the dirty-water tank, empty it and rinse it.
Lift out the wash tray and rinse it under running water.
Wipe the base of the dock dry and put the tray and the tank back.
Fill the clean-water tank if it is low.
clean_wash_dock.caution: Let the tray dry before the robot goes back onto it.

clean_dock_washing_system.title: Clean the dock washing system
clean_dock_washing_system.why: The dock's washing system flushes dirt out of the mop. Residue left in it means the mop comes out dirty.
steps: Lift the wash insert out of the dock.
Rinse it under running water and clear hair and debris from its openings.
Wipe the seat of the insert in the dock.
Put the insert back so that it sits flat.
clean_dock_washing_system.caution: No cleaning agents unless the dock's manual allows them.

clean_mop_washing_system.title: Clean the mop washing system
clean_mop_washing_system.why: The roller mop's washing system scrapes dirty water off the mop. When its openings clog, dirty water can drip onto the floor.
steps: Take the roller mop off the robot.
Rinse the scraper and its openings under running water, and clear blocked holes with a soft brush.
Rinse the roller mop and let it dry.
Fit the roller mop back until it clicks.
clean_mop_washing_system.caution: No sharp tools on the scraper's openings.

replace_filter.title: Replace the filter
replace_filter.why: A filter loses its effect over time, even when it is tapped clean regularly.
steps: Take the bin out of the robot.
Lift the old filter out by its tab.
Insert the new filter with the pleats facing the same way as the old one.
Slide the bin back in until it clicks, then mark the filter as replaced.
replace_filter.caution: Use a filter made for this model: one that does not seal lets dust through.

steps: Press the bin release and pull the bin out.
Press the old filter down and lift it out.
Put the new filter in with the pleats facing the same way as the old one.
Slide the bin in until it clicks and report the filter as replaced.
Take the bin out of the robot.
Press the tab of the filter door, lift the door and pull the old filter out by its yellow tab.
Put the new filter in with the pleats facing the same way and close the filter door.
Slide the bin in until it clicks and report the filter as replaced.
Press the bin release on the back of the robot and take the bin out.
Grip the old filter at its sides and pull it out to the left.
Put the new filter in with the pleats facing the same way as the old one.
Slide the bin into its guide until it clicks and report the filter as replaced.
Open the lid and lift the bin out by its handle.
Open the filter door and pull the old filter out by its loop.
Put the new filter in and close the filter door: it only closes with the filter seated correctly.
Put the bin back and report the filter as replaced.

replace_main_brush.title: Replace the main brushes
replace_main_brush.why: Worn brushes reach the floor less well and pick up less dirt.
steps: Turn the robot over and open the brush frame.
Lift both brushes out. Keep the end caps if the new brushes come without them.
Insert the new brushes where each shape fits, and close the frame.
Mark the brushes as replaced.
replace_main_brush.caution: The two brushes are not alike and fit only one way round. Do not force them.

steps: Turn the robot over and lift the two yellow tabs of the brush frame.
Take out the bristle brush and the beater brush. Keep the end caps if the new brushes have none.
Put in the new brushes where their shape fits and close the frame.
Report the brushes as replaced.
Turn the robot over, squeeze the yellow tabs and fold the brush frame up.
Take out both rollers. Keep the end caps if the new ones have none.
Put in the new rollers where their pegs fit and close the frame until it clicks.
Report the brushes as replaced.
Turn the robot over and press the release button next to the brushes.
Take out both rollers. Keep the end caps if the new ones have none.
Put in the new rollers where their shape fits and close the frame.
Report the brushes as replaced.
Turn the robot over and press the button on the right of the cleaning head.
Take out both rollers. Keep the end caps if the new ones have none.
Put in the new rollers where their shape fits and close the latch.
Report the brushes as replaced.

replace_side_brush.title: Replace the side brush
replace_side_brush.why: A worn side brush no longer reaches into edges and corners.
steps: Turn the robot over.
Undo the screw, or pull the old brush off its shaft.
Push the new brush onto the shaft and fasten it.
Mark the side brush as replaced.
replace_side_brush.caution: Keep the screw: a brush that sits loose falls off during cleaning.

s.title: Replace the corner brush
s.why: A worn corner brush no longer reaches into corners.
steps: Turn the robot over.
Undo the screw and take the old corner brush off.
Put the new corner brush on the peg and tighten the screw.
Report the corner brush as replaced.

replace_bag.title: Replace the bag
replace_bag.why: The bag in the station collects what the robot empties into it. When it is full, the station can no longer empty the robot.
steps: Open the lid of the station.
Pull the bag out by its tab: the tab seals the opening.
Insert the new bag and push its card into the guide until it sits.
Close the lid and mark the bag as replaced.
replace_bag.caution: Do not reuse a bag: its seal closes only once.

replace_battery.title: Replace the battery
replace_battery.why: A battery loses capacity with every charge. The robot then runs for less time and may stop before it has finished.
steps: Switch the robot off and turn it over.
Undo the screws of the battery cover and lift the cover off.
Pull the old battery out by its tabs and insert the new one with the contacts facing the same way.
Fit the cover, set the robot on the dock and mark the battery as replaced.
replace_battery.caution: Use a battery made for this model, and take the old one to a battery collection point.

replace_pad.title: Replace the mop pad
replace_pad.why: A worn pad leaves streaks and picks up less dirt.
steps: Lift the robot or take it off the dock.
Pull the old pad off its holder.
Slide or press the new pad onto the holder until it sits.
Mark the pad as replaced.
replace_pad.caution: Wash washable pads without fabric softener; use disposable pads only once.

replace_roller.title: Replace the roller mop
replace_roller.why: A worn roller mop no longer presses evenly on the floor and leaves streaks.
steps: Take the roller mop off the robot.
Fit the new roller until it clicks on both sides.
Mark the roller mop as replaced.
replace_roller.caution: Let a washed roller dry before it goes back on.

replace_detergent.title: Replace the detergent
replace_detergent.why: The station adds detergent from its cartridge to the cleaning water. When it is empty, the robot mops with water alone.
steps: Open the station's detergent compartment.
Take out the empty cartridge.
Insert the new one until it sits, and close the compartment.
Mark the detergent as replaced.
replace_detergent.caution: Use only detergent made for the station: other agents can foam or damage it.
